headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: both agents can read/write local files and run shell commands, with Open Interpreter’s broad filesystem/network access amplifying the course agent’s secret-handling surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read/write the whole filesystem and uses clipboard/stdin-stdout, while the course agent also reads/writes files and exposes API endpoints. A shared filesystem or copied outputs can let one agent’s content be treated as instructions by the other. No direct provenance or isolation is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default local setups.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through shared files or copy-paste, injected instructions can propagate.
IF either agent parses the other’s file contents as commands, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Disable clipboard bridging between agents.
Keep each agent in a separate working directory.
Require manual review of any file passed from one agent to the other.
Run one agent in a container with read-only mounts for shared inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and has broad network egress; the course agent handles configuration secrets and paper data. If they share a workspace or local files, sensitive material can flow from B into A and then out via A’s networked model-provider calls. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local directory, secrets in B’s files can be read by A.
IF A sends context to configured model providers, any leaked secrets can leave the machine.
mitigations: Store B’s secrets outside any shared workspace.
Run A with network egress disabled for secret-bearing tasks.
Use separate OS users for the two agents.
Rotate any secrets that may have been exposed in shared files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, install packages, read and write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. Open Interpreter also modifies git state, while the course agent runs via docker compose in a local dev environment. Concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can corrupt files or git state; no locking is documented, so conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or directory, simultaneous writes can race.
IF either agent performs git operations while the other edits files, repository state can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the same path.
Avoid concurrent git operations.
Use file locks for shared mutable resources.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination primitives.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate shell actions and file edits, and the course agent exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints that may consume prior outputs. If B treats A’s generated text or files as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into downstream actions. The pathway exists in default local workflows, but B’s action authority is narrower than a full admin agent, so medium fits.
conditions: IF B ingests A’s generated text without verification, errors can propagate.
IF A’s outputs are used as prompts or source material for B’s agentic endpoints, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Require human review before B consumes A’s outputs.
Separate factual outputs from executable instructions.
Add validation checks on any A-produced files before B uses them.
Limit B to read-only analysis when fed A’s content.
requires-engineering: implement provenance and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: The course agent explicitly handles configuration secrets and academic data, while Open Interpreter can access anything on the local machine and send context to model providers. If regulated or sensitive course data is processed on the same machine, retention and residency expectations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared local environment, both agents may retain or transmit it differently.
IF organizational policy requires specific residency or retention controls, the profiles do not show them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Review retention settings for any model-provider integrations.
Use separate storage for secrets and research artifacts.
Document which agent may process which data class.
requires-engineering: align both agents to a common compliance policy.
